reason: Correct on the grep, wrong about what the artifact is, and the fix would damage the direction's best idea. (1) Category error. master.html is a state renderer, not an app shell: data-state is set from the URL, each state declares a medium and carries a caption naming it as a medium ('Print / A4, the keepsake'), and the Design Console is the browsing surface. Five of the twelve brief-mandated states have no in-artifact control aimed at them -- unfurl (a chat card, which by construction cannot have one), ended, loading, loading-slow and owner-empty. The finding's principle, 'a designed object with no entrance is the same as a missing state', condemns all five. The brief lists conditions to draw and grade ('they grade differently, so they are separate states'), not a navigation graph; 'the printed keepsake ... is in scope' means draw it and grade it, and the finding itself concedes it is the best-composed artifact in the set. The wired transitions that do exist (Preview, Publish, Back to the plan) are there because those sequences are themselves designed moments, not because the lab exposes a menu of states. (2) The guest half of the fix is impossible as written and would make the work worse. Driven at 1440x960 and 1280x900, phone, desk, day and print return exactly zero focusable elements, and states.desk has no header to add to -- only a .b-previewStrip that appears when cameFromOwner, with the source comment 'Loading this state directly is byte-identical to what a guest gets.' The fix therefore asks to invent app chrome on the received artifact and make a Print button the only control an audience ever sees, on the one surface whose whole thesis (DIRECTIONS A and B: 'the received artifact is not a timeline, it is a printed programme', 'a thing you are sent') is that it is an object and not an operating surface. That is a net loss at a 9.5 bar, not a gain. (3) The owner half is misplaced on its own terms. Add a moment / Preview / Publish is a build-check-send arc with a single primary at the end; dropping a post-publish, morning-of act between Preview and Publish breaks that arc and dilutes the ceremony the direction names as its loudest moment. A fourth control costs the bar's legibility to expose something the browser already has a learned, universal command for. (4) The door for a piece of paper already exists and works: '@page { size: A4; margin: 0 }' plus the @media print block that zeroes .tl-page padding, hides .tl-caption and unclamps the sheet stage exist precisely so Ctrl+P on the keepsake yields a correct one-page A4 -- I generated the PDF and it does; the code comments record the two-sheet defect that plumbing was written to fix. That work only makes sense because the intended entrance is the print command, not a button.
sharpenedFix: Not a change this verdict asks for. If a product route to the keepsake is ever wanted downstream, the correct shape is not a fourth button: make the guest page's own @media print rendering resolve to the sheet, so Ctrl+P from phone or desk produces the keepsake and the audience artifact keeps its zero controls. That is a build decision for the shipping app, not a defect in this lab.
